lots.guide_summary: Close SOLD entries (modern and older McCulloch petrol saws at Gowans, last 12 months) range from $46 to $100 hammer, plus one close UNSOLD (M4218 passed in, then sold at $50). Wider category guide entries (budget-brand and old McCulloch saws) run $15 to $65. All are SOLD hammer prices except the one passed-in M4218. No ASKING evidence: the WebSearch cap was hit, so no retail or Armitage past results were checked. All AUD, no conversion.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD = $46 (Gowans 376752, modern McCulloch, same styling). $46 / 1.22 = $37.70, rounded down to $35 hammer ($42.70 all-in). Flip: likely resale about $50 locally (the $46 and $50 modern McCulloch results), less about 10% selling fees ($5) and $0 postage (sell as local pickup, too awkward to post), net $45. $45 / 2.44 = $18.44, rounded down to $15 hammer. The $100 result was an older pro saw with a fuel can, so it is not used to set the cap.
lots.confidence_reason: Badge read clearly in photo 2. SOLD comparators opened (API records and photos), but none is an M4620 itself, and running condition is unknown.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped the researcher's aggregated 'comparators $30 to $55' entry: it rolled about 10 lots into one line with a made-up midpoint ($40). I re-checked the ids in the API, and the figures are real, so I split out two individual lots (Ryobi 377808, Oleo Mac 431240) as category guide entries. Dropped the empty 'ASKING not found' placeholder. Dropped 365158 (Ozito drop saw, nail gun and McCulloch motor only, a mixed lot) and 439907 (McCulloch plus NuPower, two saws, models unknown) as not comparable. Moved 403942 (sale_price 0) to UNSOLD.
lots.key_photo_findings: Badge reads McCulloch M4620 Made in USA. Bar and chain fitted, chain looks intact, with the scabbard present. Plastics show light scuffing and dirt, and there is some debris visible behind the cooling vents. No obvious cracks or missing parts in the two photos. Pull cord and handle are visible. Fuel or oil level and compression are unknown.
lots.condition: Used, appears complete with bar, chain and cover. Light wear and dirt. Running condition unknown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Does it start and run, and does it have compression? Is the chain sharp, and has the chain brake been checked? Is there fuel or oil in it?

lots.guide_summary: All SOLD Gowans hammers, last 13 months. Similar mixed tin lots made $9 to $60 and the closest single can (Vacuum Oil Pegasus 4 gallon) made $65. Components: common Mobil tins $7.50 to $20 each, plain cast kettles $15 to $30 (top $50), Titan Nails crate about $5 (2 boxes for $10). No result was found for the Careel or Alfa-Laval tins or the Turner mower can, which are the better pieces. No UNSOLD or ASKING evidence. The WebSearch cap was hit, so no Armitage results. Range used: $15 to $65 AUD, no conversion.
lots.working: No SOLD result for this lot or anything like it as a whole. The SOLD evidence is component and category level only. A rough sum of parts from the Gowans hammers (Mobil tin about $10, crate about $5, kettle about $20, plus three tins with no evidence) suggests about $60 to $120 hammer, but that is a guide, not a same-item sale. So maximum bids are 0 under the rules.
lots.confidence_reason: Labels read clearly, but there is no same-item SOLD for the mixed lot, and no evidence at all for the Careel, Alfa-Laval or Turner can, which drive the value.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. All researcher ids were re-checked in the Gowans API and match title, price and date. The researcher's URL for the 2025-11-24 crate lot lacked an id, so I found it (377749). I added Gowans 379512 (Cascade and Titan Nails boxes, $10).
lots.key_photo_findings: Gargoyle Mobiloil B tin: heavily rubbed, rust spotted and dirty, with a cork-type stopper. Alfa-Laval Separator Oil tin: green, good graphics with some rubbing. Careel tin: strong farm graphic, some wear, but a price tag is stuck over part of the name. Mobilgas Turner Four-Stroke Rotary Mower can: graphics mostly clear, scuffed. Titan Nail & Wire South Melbourne crate: stencil legible, sound. Cast iron kettle: heavy surface rust, lid present.
lots.condition: Dusty and rubbed with rust spotting. Graphics mostly intact on the Careel, Alfa-Laval and Mobilgas tins. The kettle is rusty.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you check for holes or rust-through in the tins (bases especially), whether the Careel tin is still sealed or holding any contents (it is labelled poisonous), and whether the tag can come off without damaging the label?
